Hello, all. I'm trying to proof of concept some better methods for our company. We currently document everything on a wiki. However, our system is very complex with many interdependencies. We currently use Jira for ticketing, and Redbeam for asset management. It would be extremely helpful to integrate a CMDB into this, so changes, or incidents can be linked back to dependencies. We had tried numerous things to track and manage change, but they all fell down in the one part that is necessary: end user adoption (and management sabotage).

We got lucky and I found the open source iTop. It's ITIL compliant (although it has a 'relaxed' mode available if you don't want to be as insanely formal as full ITIL), ticketing, asset tracking, change tracking, and approval system. It's the most user friendly open source CMDB I have found. We previously had RT ITIL and it was so formal no one wanted to use it.

Hey all, just wanted to get your input if you have nay on this kind of treatment? I have been in traditional talk therapy for 3 years now and while it has been great getting me this far I started to look into what can help me control the anxiety better everyday.
Starting CBT with Psycho-dynamic therapy on Friday for long term Panic disorder. Anyone have any experience with it?

I've done CBT before, but not psycho-dynamic therapy. I can tell you that CBT is a good way to go if you feel you're ready. It's a lot more daunting than traditional talk therapy and includes a lot of real world experience and things like that. It's less "What's wrong?" and more "Here's how you fix it." For example I hate walking in public and one of the exercises my therapist did with me was take me out for walks. It's also about self therapy; about handling the problems on your own and becoming more independent.

Overall I would say it's a great thing to do if you are ready to move on. I'd say you are after three years of traditional talk therapy. Good luck with it. You'll be kicking ass in no time.

Thanks for the response, I read a bit about CBT and figured it was going to be a lot more active in facing my fear. If only my mind would remember how many times I have done these things already without dying ha ha ha

I have experience, but not in the same way. I worked residential treatment that was CBT based. The whole concept of establishing an emotional baseline, recognizing it and knowing how to positively change your behavior is astounding in it's effectiveness. It may be a bit of a shock at first, since it's behavior based, but once you're able to see the cycle and start connecting the thoughts to the feelings to the behaviors, you will be a lot more self-reliant and confident in what you do.

If you have any questions I'd be happy to answer, otherwise I wish you the best of luck.
Thanks BeerBaron, I'm more excited than nervous about it I think.
That's a good place to be. I hope it helps.

I am currently in school for Metal Health Counseling and CBT is all the rage for getting things done. It helps to alter the negative thoughts and behaviors rather than simply talk about them. It seems to be one of the most effective types at helping people gain some control over themselves.

Thanks little_raindrop, I am a firm believer that my anxiety is cause by negative thoughts running loose in my mind and years of compounding them going without treatment.

Here's hoping it the beginning of the end for that : )

I had long term panic disorder, and I did CBT, but not sure about the pscyho-dynamic aspect of it. It was amazing. I haven't attended a session in 6 years, but I'm still over one of my biggest triggers, which was the feeling of being dizzy. After a few sessions of talking about it, my doctor gave me homework of sitting in an office chair and spinning it in circles for a short period of time, and then using the skills he'd taught me to be aware of how the dizziness triggered my anxiety and how to deal with it. I got up to spinning in that chair for two minutes, getting dizzy as hell, then just feeling no anxiety about it. It really stuck with me, too. Now when I feel dizzy from being anxious, it doesn't trigger panic. It was extremely liberating. I think you'll really appreciate the outcome of this type of therapy. Really, really try to do your assignments, though, because the more you do the faster it works, and longer it sticks because you end up reinforcing the things you've learned on a daily basis. Good luck, and congrats on making it so far! I know it's hell.
Thanks HeyTalina, It's so encouraging to hear people having success with it.
